content: Individuals who are candidates for metabolic surgery are at an elevated risk of developing or experiencing exacerbations of substance abuse, depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation. This risk is particularly pronounced if these mental health issues worsen following the surgical procedure. It is essential that all candidates undergo a comprehensive mental health evaluation conducted by a qualified professional with expertise in managing obesity-related conditions prior to surgery. If a candidate is found to have unresolved substance abuse issues or severe mental health disorders, the surgical procedure should be postponed until these concerns are adequately addressed and managed. Both preoperative and postoperative psychological assessments are indispensable in ensuring the safety and overall well-being of the patient throughout the surgical process and recovery period.
